examination: Civil Services Mains Examination - Optional Subject
document_type: Official Syllabus, Political Science and International Relations Paper II
provenance_note: Unit text is the published UPSC syllabus for PSIR Paper II, corroborated across independent reproductions. It has NOT been diffed against the UPSC notification PDF. Verify before promoting any mention to verified; the syllabus does not change year to year, so one check settles it permanently.
structure_note: The official syllabus divides this paper into Section A (Comparative Politics and International Relations) and Section B (India and the World). Those parts are carried per node in section_ref rather than as topic rows - the ingest supports only topic -> microtopic, and spending the top level on a binary split would leave the corpus tagging against two buckets.
paper_title_note: paper_title MUST match the existing subjects.name for slug upsc-cse-mains-opt-psir-p2 exactly. resolve_subject() in the ingest script searches by name; a mismatch creates a duplicate subject with a hash-suffixed slug and orphans the whole spine. This happened on Paper-I.

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: Comparative Politics: nature and major approaches
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: Comparative Politics: Nature and major approaches; political economy and political sociology perspectives; limitations of the comparative method.
micro_themes: Nature and scope of comparative politics; major approaches
Political economy perspective in comparative analysis
Political sociology perspective in comparative analysis
Limitations of the comparative method
Institutional approach and its successive criticisms

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: State in comparative perspective: Characteristics and changing nature of the State in capitalist and socialist economies, and advanced industrial and developing societies.
micro_themes: Characteristics and changing nature of the State in capitalist economies
The State in socialist economies
The State in advanced industrial societies
The State in developing societies

micro_themes: Political parties in advanced industrial societies

micro_themes: Responses to globalisation from developed societies
Responses to globalisation from developing societies
